name: Casa da Música
short: Rem Koolhaas's concert hall on Rotunda da Boavista, opened in 2005 and home to the Porto orchestra.
long: Casa da Música is Portugal's first concert hall conceived from the outset exclusively for music — public performance, training and creation. It stands on the Rotunda da Boavista, on the site of a former tram terminus. Its asymmetric white-concrete polyhedron, cut by wavy glazing, has become a symbol of modern Porto. Inside are the roughly 1,238-seat Suggia Hall, Sala 2 and an azulejo-clad VIP hall.
history:
In the late 1990s Porto was preparing to become European Capital of Culture for 2001. In 1998 the Ministry of Culture announced the construction of Casa da Música, and in 1999 the international competition was won by the project of Rem Koolhaas and his office OMA.

The site on the Rotunda da Boavista, a former tram terminus, was chosen in 1999. The engineers were Arup (London) and Afassociados (Porto), and the interiors were designed by Petra Blaisse (Inside Outside). The unusual form complicated construction, and the building cost around 100 million euros.

The building opened to the public on 14 April 2005 with concerts by Clã and Lou Reed, and the official inauguration followed on 15 April in the presence of the president and prime minister, with a performance by the Porto National Orchestra. Casa da Música immediately became a city icon.

The main hall is named after the Porto-born cellist Guilhermina Suggia. It is known for its flexible acoustics and its two glass walls — the only concert hall in the world with such a feature. Its programme ranges from symphonic concerts to jazz, world music and contemporary electronica.

The Casa da Música Foundation was established in 2006. Besides the Porto orchestra, the building houses the Remix Ensemble, a baroque orchestra and choirs. The foundation's educational and social projects — Som da Rua, Mundi, A Casa Vai a Casa — involve thousands of participants every year.
facts: Designed by Rem Koolhaas and OMA after an international competition in 1999.
Opened on 14–15 April 2005 as part of Porto's European Capital of Culture 2001 programme.
The Suggia Hall seats about 1,238 and is named after cellist Guilhermina Suggia.
The only concert hall in the world with two entirely glass walls.
Construction cost about 100 million euros; the form is a nine-floor asymmetric white-concrete polyhedron.
Interiors were designed by Petra Blaisse (Inside Outside), and the VIP hall is clad in azulejo tiles.
It is home to the Orquestra Sinfónica do Porto Casa da Música (formerly Orquestra Nacional do Porto).
tip: The foyer and open terrace can be visited for free; listings and tickets are at casadamusica.com. The easiest way to get there is the metro to Casa da Música station.
